newsitem.title: USA: Unocal CEO says better focus improved earns.
newsitem.headline: Unocal CEO says better focus improved earns.

text.p: Unocal Corp's better first quarter earnings were a result of improved focus of the business after the sale of its West Coast downstream operations and higher production of crude, condensate, and natural gas in the Far East, the company's chief executive said Thursday.

"We continued to show increased natural gas production in the first quarter, reflecting the success of our focus on key strategic projects in Southeast Asia," said Roger C. Beach, Unocal chairman and chief executive officer, in a statement announcing earnings.
Unocal reported first quarter 1997 net earnings of $144 million or $0.57 per common share up 16 percent from $124 million or $0.47 per share in the same period a year ago.

Beach noted that the first quarter operating results reflect significantly higher average sales prices for crude oil and natural gas. Worldwide, Unocal's average sales price for crude and condensate was $20.81 per barrel, compared with $16.93 in 1996, while the sales price for natural gas averaged $2.51 per thousand cubic feet, compared with $2.27 for the same period last year.
